steps.note: S1.1.1.a states that rows 0-1 subtract the old scratch contributions, rows 2-5 add the source effect and rows 6-7 restore the scratch, so the net target change is (JV+RG)x independent of the initial scratch values; this matches the paper.
S1.1.1.b gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, says the side contribution cancels exactly the intersection-one cases, and gives self coefficient one, as the paper does.
S1.1.1.c gives the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, has the side wires cancel intersections zero and two, and notes that intersection one contributes zero, matching the paper.
S1.1.2 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), with each invocation restoring its own auxiliary wires.

The plan lists gate and data-wire labels (S1.3.3, S1.3.4) and says every edge joins comparable labels (S1.3.5), but it never gives the per-edge orthogonal residuals and their dimensions (the residual table); it gives only the centre 3->4 residual P tensor F.

S1.3.1 notes that neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal, but the plan never treats the side edge 2->5: the inclusion <t_X> in t_Y^perp and the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2 are missing.

The plan states that the only decreasing edges are centre 3->4, each losing h (S1.3.5), that sources sum to N, sinks to Wm-N and the signed total telescopes to Wm-2N (S1.3.2), and that the Ic losses give L=Ich and absolute total Wm-2N+2L (S1.3.6).

S1.3.5 only asserts that every nonzero binary residual has an orthonormal basis; it omits why: that each residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating over F_2, and the step that absorbs alternating planes.
S1.3.7 gives exactly L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539.

S1.4.2 gives the identity wt(z+w)=wt(z)+wt(w)-2|supp cap supp|, weight additive mod 4 on orthogonal vectors, and q_V-q_U as the sum of wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal basis of the residual, negated on a decreasing edge.
S1.4.3 states that wt(v) is odd, so the phase is i^{eps[v.x]}, and that H diag(1,-1) H = X turns the character into the translation X_v, giving aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The interface step S1.4 leaves out the k-column tensoring, but S3.1 states it: on f columns, each residual slot h <= rho_edge gives one child (C^{eps_h})^{tensor f}, conjugated column by column by P_M. S1.4.4 counts s_c kernels over the network. I also checked paper lines 1867-1890; credit rests on S3.1.

S1.4.5 gives frames I and C^{tensor m} for the zero and full labels and C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) for X_a->Y_a. S1.4.6 gives the Z_{a,k}-before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k}-after repair via C=iZC^{-1}Z, and the negation of the physical X outputs.
S1.3 and S1.3.7 state L/N<1/2 for both networks; S1.3.8.b states the deficit N-2L_b>0, so s_b<W_b m; S1.4.4 states the complex deficit 2N-2L_c>0. I also checked lines 1162-1167.
S1.5.1 gives eta_b=(W_b m-s_b)/(W_b m)=339/22587335000000, matching the paper.
S1.5.1 gives eta_c=(W_c m-s_c)/(W_c m)=73/19906842167500, matching the paper.
S1.5.2 states that both deficits exceed 20*2^{-50}. S1.5.3 uses log m<20 to get m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta), hence s/W<m^tau, and S1.5 sets tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}.

S2.1.1.a-c give the elimination proof as the paper does: pivot at the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row, clearing by lower-triangular elementary operations, repetition on the active indices, exactly a ones, and E_1=L^{-1}, E_2=R^{-1}.

S2.1 only names 'a suitable fixed odd prime q'. The plan never says the prime avoids every denominator (and diagonal numerator) in a finite table of factors, so it never shows why the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.

S2.1.2 states that a lower-triangular transformation costs O(V), updating coordinates in descending physical order by a unit multiple plus earlier unchanged coordinates, with lower-triangular inverses.
S2.1.4 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, the interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j for each one of Pi. S2.1.5 states one interchange per one and a in all.
S3.5 states E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, C_0=128mB^2, C_1=20 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}). It omits nu and the general rule C_1=max{20,nu+3}, but it gives C_1 at the value the paper uses here.

The plan never states the arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e)<=8e at a leaf, nor the per-invocation operation count below E. S3.5 only says Delta bounds denominator and magnitude growth.
The unrolling B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu, the bound A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and the total below C_0 d^{C_1} are all missing from the plan.

S3.5 gives the fractional width p+Delta and Delta=o(p) from eps*C_1<1. It omits the depth-ell induction (values in 2^{-(p+ell)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^ell) that makes this reservation exact, and the Delta+3 integer bits, so the result is asserted without the sub-step's mechanism.
S3.6 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disk arrays map to disk arrays and the final truncation errs by less than sqrt2*2^{-p}.

summary: 19 of 26 sub-steps present, none wrong. All bank-exchange (B1-B4), phase-interface (P1-P4) and rank-saving (R1-R4) steps are present, P3 only through the layer step S3.1. Absent: the residual table (L1), the side-edge 2->5 argument (L2), the nonalternating/orthonormal-basis argument (L4, whose result is asserted without derivation), the denominator-avoiding prime (M2), and the guard-width recurrence, its unrolling and the depth-to-width induction (S2-S4). S1's constants appear without nu.
